ConsoleWindowManager

ConsoleWindowManager manages the console session, root elements, input and rendering. It runs the UI on one thread, so changes to attached controls need to happen on that thread.

Running the Window

Creating a window does not change the terminal. RunAsync starts the loop and completes after it stops and restores the terminal. Run is available if you need a blocking call instead. Do not start another run while one is already active.

Title sets the console window or terminal title where supported. It does not add a heading to the UI. Headings and status messages should be normal controls.

Updating the UI from Other Threads

Use Post or InvokeAsync to change attached controls from background work:

  • Post(Action): Queues an action without waiting for it. Unhandled errors use the window's exception event.
  • InvokeAsync(Action): Queues an action and returns a task you can await. An exception in the action faults that task.
  • CheckAccess: Reports whether the current thread is allowed to access the UI.

These methods are only available while RunAsync is active and the window has not started stopping. Stop your background producers before disposing the window.

Keep the queued action short. Do file access, network requests and other slow work outside it. An async lambda passed as an Action becomes async void, so it should not be used to represent awaited background work.

Window Events

  • Updating: Called for recurring UI updates at the configured rate. Keep handlers short.
  • FrameRendered: Called when a frame is actually presented. FrameNumber is the current sequence number.
  • UnhandledException: Reports unexpected posted, keyboard and render/update callback errors.

TargetFrameRate is the target update rate. It does not guarantee that every update writes a new frame; an unchanged cached frame may not be presented again.

The file is read before the UI action is queued. Compile returns false for invalid markup, leaving the previous page in place. A failure to read the file is a separate error for the application to handle.

Handling Errors

If an unexpected error is not handled, RunAsync faults after terminal cleanup. InvokeAsync actions report their errors through their own returned task.

Do not write directly to Console while the UI is running. Use a TextBlock, a log control, or your application's logger instead.
